scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC3 (10.3.0.100) in Office B reports it cannot reach anything outside its own
subnet -- no Internet, no Office A, no Server Room -- though it can still reach
other hosts on its own VLAN. Other Office B hosts are unaffected. PC3 was working
before a desktop reconfiguration. Diagnose.

injection.action: point PC3's default route at a non-existent in-subnet gateway
injection.command:
ip route del default 2>/dev/null
  ip route add default via 10.3.0.99

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: pc3 default-gateway configuration
Mechanism: PC3's correct gateway is 10.3.0.1 (its VLAN SVI/VRRP VIP). It was
  reconfigured to 10.3.0.99, which is inside PC3's subnet but is not assigned to
  any device, so ARP for the gateway never resolves and PC3 cannot forward any
  off-subnet traffic. Same-subnet hosts remain reachable (direct ARP), which is
  why intra-VLAN traffic still works.
Localization: pc3
Root cause: PC3's default gateway set to 10.3.0.99 instead of 10.3.0.1
Fix: restore PC3's default route -- `ip route add default via 10.3.0.1`
scenario.fix_spec: restore PC3's default route -- `ip route add default via 10.3.0.1`

results.actual:
PING 10.1.0.100 (10.1.0.100) 56(84) bytes of data.

--- 10.1.0.100 ping statistics ---
2 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss, time 1066ms

agent.diagnosis_text:
PC3 (10.3.0.100/24) is the only affected device because its default gateway is
misconfigured. The host is pointing to 10.3.0.99 as its gateway, but that address
does not exist anywhere in the topology: an ARP request for 10.3.0.99 returns
"FAILED" and three pings to that address yield 100% packet loss. Because no
on-subnet device owns 10.3.0.99, PC3 cannot resolve where to send inter-subnet
traffic, so all packets destined outside 10.3.0.0/24 are dropped at the first hop.
Intra-VLAN traffic still works because it does not require ARP resolution of the
gateway — frames are sent directly to the destination MAC on the same segment.

The correct default gateway for the 10.3.0.0/24 (Office B) subnet is 10.3.0.1,
which is a HSRP/VRRP virtual IP held by dswb1 (confirmed reachable: 0% loss,
MAC 02:80:31:d5:1d:ff). dswb1 carries 10.3.0.1/32 + 10.3.0.2/24 on br0.10,
and dswb2 carries 10.3.0.3/24 on the same VLAN. All other Office B devices use
this VIP correctly; only PC3 is affected.

Root cause: the "desktop reconfiguration" manually changed PC3's default gateway
from 10.3.0.1 to the non-existent address 10.3.0.99.

Corrective fix: on PC3, delete the bad default route and restore the correct one:
  ip route del default
  ip route add default via 10.3.0.1 dev eth0
For persistence, update /etc/network/interfaces (or the appropriate ifupdown/
netplan stanza) so the change survives a reboot.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names PC3 (10.3.0.100/24) as the sole affected device and describes a host-side default-gateway misconfiguration.
The agent explicitly identifies PC3's default gateway/default route as misconfigured (set to 10.3.0.99) and recommends restoring the default via 10.3.0.1.
Correctly instructs removal of the bad default route and adding the default via 10.3.0.1 (with persistence), which matches the expected fix.

The agent's logs show PC3's route/gateway and failed pings to 10.3.0.99 plus successful pings to the real VIP 10.3.0.1 and switch IP allocations, and the writeup's claims follow directly from those observations. The conclusion that PC3's misconfigured gateway (10.3.0.99) causes loss of off-subnet connectivity is well-supported and the recommended fix is appropriate.
